prerequisites: Having studied and passed the basic "Graphic Expression" course from the first year, as the knowledge acquired, especially regarding Computer-Aided Design, is essential.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply Representation Systems, being able to transfer shapes, surfaces, volumes, elements, and mechanical systems from space to plane, and vice versa.
Be able to relate the aforementioned applied knowledge with that of the different scientific disciplines typical of other subjects in their study plan.
Appreciate the importance of standardization as a means of universalizing graphical language.

Acquire proficiency in sketching drawings as a means of graphically expressing ideas quickly, improvisationally, and very effectively. It is the usual means of communication between the engineer and the operator in the workshop or factory.
Value the technical language of Industrial Drawing as the ideal tool to express their future creations, designs, and technical projects.
Know how to interpret and generate assembly drawings using CAD resources, distinguishing between the functions of each element.
Instill the idea that a part or component almost never makes sense on its own but must always be considered as part of the assembly or mechanism to which it belongs.

Extend the concept of standardization beyond "Drawing Standards," showing that mass production has also introduced standardization related to shapes and dimensions of elements. Introduce the use of these standards.

Present certain elements very common in industry (threads, keys, gears, bearings, welding, etc.). Know what they are and what they are used for. Know their representation in drawings. Know the standardization of these elements and the use of catalogs.
Acquire the conceptual bases on the functioning and possibilities of computers in the field of Graphic Engineering.
At the end of the course, students must have the ability to address new disciplines in the study plan, especially subjects that require the use of graphic expression techniques.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Capacity for the use of scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for the search for sustainable engineering solutions.
Capacity for teamwork and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Capacity to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, on the basis of the training acquired and necessary for the evolution of technique.
Knowledge and capacities to apply graphic engineering techniques.

syllabus_topics: Flexible Transmissions by Belts, Chains, and Cables
Representation of Assemblies and Exploded Views
teaching_methods: Theoretical academic sessions (lectures with computer support)
Practical sessions in the computer lab (problem formulation, analysis, resolution, and debate)
Practical sessions in the classroom (practical exercises related to theoretical content)
Problem solving (sketching and CAD exercises, some mandatory for submission)
Objective tests (multiple-choice or short-answer questionnaires, in-person or via Studium platform)

assessment_methods.method: Questionnaires (in-person and/or via online platform during the course)
Development of practical cases (on specified dates during the course)

assessment_rules: Each questionnaire will count towards the final grade only if the score obtained is 5 or higher. It is essential to obtain a minimum of 35% in each of the assessed items to pass the course. For the second call (resit), there will be a final exam on a date specified by the Center, accounting for 100% of the course grade.
